what_its_for: Rotigotine is used to treat Parkinson's disease (a condition that causes shaking, stiffness, and slow movement) and Restless Legs Syndrome (RLS), which causes uncomfortable feelings in your legs and an urge to move them, especially at night. It works by acting like a natural chemical in your brain called dopamine.
how_to_take: Rotigotine comes as a patch that you stick on your skin. Apply one patch every 24 hours (once a day) at the same time each day. Choose a clean, dry area of skin that is not irritated, cut, or oily — good spots include your belly, thigh, hip, shoulder, or upper arm. Press the patch firmly onto your skin for about 30 seconds. Do NOT cut the patch. Rotate the application site each day so you are not using the same spot within 14 days. Remove the old patch before putting on a new one. Fold the used patch in half (sticky sides together) and dispose of it safely, away from children and pets.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks. For Parkinson's disease, the starting dose is usually one 2 mg/24-hour patch daily, and it may be increased gradually up to a maximum of 16 mg/24-hour patch. For Restless Legs Syndrome, the usual starting dose is one 1 mg/24-hour patch daily, which may be increased up to a maximum of 3 mg/24-hour patch. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you forget to change your patch at your usual time, apply a new patch as soon as you remember and change it at your regular time the next day. If you forget to apply a patch entirely for one day, apply a new patch the next day at your normal scheduled time. Do NOT use two patches at once to make up for a missed dose. Call your doctor if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store unused patches at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep patches in their original sealed pouches and do not open until you are ready to use them. Keep all patches away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used patches by folding them sticky-side together and throwing them in the trash — never flush them down the toilet unless instructed to do so.
what_to_avoid: Avoid exposing the patch to direct heat sources such as heating pads, electric blankets, hot tubs, saunas, or prolonged sunlight, as heat can cause too much medication to enter your body at once. Avoid applying the patch to skin that is red, irritated, or broken. Do not use the same skin spot more than once every 14 days. Avoid drinking alcohol while using this medication, as it may increase dizziness or drowsiness. Be careful driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, since it can cause sudden sleepiness or dizziness. Tell your doctor about all medications, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some drugs can interact with rotigotine.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: sudden or unusual urge to sleep during daily activities (such as driving), hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), severe confusion or unusual behavior, unusual strong urges such as gambling, overeating, or sexual urges, fainting or very low blood pressure when standing up (feeling dizzy or lightheaded), severe skin reactions at the patch site (blistering, swelling, or rash spreading beyond the patch area), swelling of your hands, feet, or legs, worsening of your symptoms, or any signs of allergic reaction such as difficulty breathing, rash, or swelling of the face or throat.
when_it_works: Rotigotine does not work right away. It may take several weeks before you notice an improvement in your symptoms, especially since your doctor will gradually increase your dose. For Parkinson's disease, it helps reduce shaking, stiffness, and slow movement over time. For Restless Legs Syndrome, many patients notice some relief within a few weeks. Be patient and do not stop using the patch without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause your symptoms to return or worsen.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): You may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness, confusion, or falls. Use with caution and report any unusual symptoms to your doctor. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. This medication should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed, as it may affect a developing baby. Breastfeeding: Rotigotine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while using this patch. Children: Rotigotine is not approved for use in children. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. MRI scans: Remove your rotigotine patch before having an MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) scan because the patch contains aluminum and can cause skin burns during the scan. Put on a new patch after the scan is complete.
